text.p: Luxembourg banned on Friday the import and sale of genetically modified maize on its territory, the Health Ministry said in a statement.
Luxembourg cited article 16 of an EU directive allowing member states to take protective action on health or environmental grounds.

"Why was the decision also to authorise imports, which is of great public concern, taken so quickly and without waiting for the results of studies on the long term implications of these products," Health Minister Johny Lahure said.
Lahure said that a surveillance system and a consumer information campaign must be set up and that importers must label all genetically modified products before they could be authorised.
Austria has also introduced a national ban.

The Luxembourg and Austrian bans follow a French ruling this week allowing the marketing of genetically modified maize developed by Swiss firm Ciba Geigy AG CIGZn.S and imported from the United States.
France obtained approval from the the European Commission in December for the marketing of gene-maize in Europe.
